_sources.discrepancies: NCSL lists AR as 'photo ID requested' (non-strict); SoS site confirms voters without photo ID may sign an affidavit and cast a regular ballot. Consistent. 2026-06-10: Corrected the 2026 primary to March 3, 2026 and the primary runoff to March 31, 2026 (this file previously listed May 19 / June 16) per the Arkansas SoS 2026 election calendar; registration deadline for the primary was February 2, 2026. Note: beginning in 2026 voters registered with one party may not vote in the other party's primary (per the Association of Arkansas Counties), tightening Arkansas's traditionally open primary.

earlyVoting.notes: Early voting for the March 3 preferential primary ran February 17 – March 2, 2026 (early voting ends at 5:00 p.m. on the Monday before Election Day). Hours vary by county.
Early voting for the March 31 primary runoff ran March 24–30, 2026 (runoff early voting begins 7 days before the election and ends the Monday before).
Early voting begins 15 days before the general election (October 19, 2026) and ends at 5:00 p.m. on the Monday before Election Day (November 2). Hours vary by county.
Early voting runs for 15 days before the general election and ends at 5:00 p.m. on the Monday before Election Day. Hours vary by county.

acceptedIds: Arkansas driver's license or state ID card
Student ID from an Arkansas public college or university (with photo and address)
Any document issued by the federal, state, or local government that shows name and photo
votingRules.expirationRule: Photo ID may be used if it is unexpired or has been expired no more than 4 years before the date of the election.
votingRules.impedimentDeclaration: If a voter does not have an acceptable photo ID, they may sign an affidavit and cast a regular (non-provisional) ballot.
votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: Arkansas prohibits use of wireless communication devices in the polling area. Voters may not photograph their ballot.
additionalRules: Open primary: any registered voter may choose which party's primary to participate in; party registration is not required.
Runoff rule: a voter who participated in one party's primary may only vote in that party's runoff.

eligibility: Will be unavoidably absent from the county on Election Day
Caregiving responsibilities for an ill or disabled person
Scheduled to work all poll hours on Election Day
voteByMail.applicationDeadline: Must be received by the county clerk 7 days before the election
voteByMail.returnDeadline: Must be received by the county clerk by 7:30 p.m. on Election Day
voteByMail.returnDeadlinePlain: Absentee ballot must arrive at the county clerk by poll closing on Election Day. Postmarks do not count.

runoffRules.ruleExplanation: Arkansas rule: if you voted in one party's primary, you can only vote in that same party's runoff. If you did not vote in the primary, you may choose either party's runoff.

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: Arkansas has an open primary (Ark. Code §7-7-301). Any registered voter may participate in either party's primary. If a runoff occurs and you voted in a party's primary, party-lock rules apply.
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: Arkansas tiene una primaria abierta (Ark. Code §7-7-301). Cualquier votante registrado puede participar en la primaria de cualquier partido. Si hay una segunda vuelta y votó en la primaria de un partido, se aplican las reglas de bloqueo de partido.
